overview: Each submission triggers an isolated function per language runtime; results pushed via WebSocket.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative workload: 100 submissions/s, 5 s average execution.
estimation.result: At 256 MB per sandbox, 500 slots need about 128 GB isolated memory.
estimation.implication: Scale by queue age and runtime; maintain hard CPU, memory, disk, process and network limits.

entityDetails.purpose: Submission identity, code location and authoritative verdict.
accessPatterns: Create idempotently; poll verdict; conditionally claim and finish execution.
constraints: A stale worker cannot overwrite a newer execution attempt; enforce fencing/version.
relationships: problem_id plus test_version pins the immutable TestBundle used for judging.

entityDetails.purpose: Versioned hidden test inputs and expected outputs.
accessPatterns: Workers fetch a pinned test version.
constraints: Tests are readable by isolated trusted workers, never by submitted code or clients.
relationships: Submissions pin a version so retries cannot silently use a changed test bundle.

apiDetails.purpose: Persist source and schedule sandboxed judging.
apiDetails.rationale: Publish execution only after the submission record is durable; enforce user quotas.
Poll with backoff or use a notification hint; hidden test details must remain private.

failureCases.scenario: A sandbox times out or a judge crashes
failureCases.handling: Kill the entire process tree/microVM, reclaim resources and persist an execution outcome. Redeliver infrastructure failures by submission_id; a user-code timeout is a verdict, not an infinite retry.

alternatives: Use workers for tight runtime and sandbox control. Use isolated serverless execution for bounded jobs that fit runtime and isolation limits; both require durable verdicts and retry fencing.
